completed.4.13: x402 wire-format fix for OKX.AI re-review (rejected with 'x402 standard validation' on first submit). Three issues in the 402 challenge emitted by @okxweb3/x402-express: (a) resource.url was http:// behind the Railway proxy — added `app.set('trust proxy', true)` so X-Forwarded-Proto sets req.protocol; (b) paymentMiddleware writes the PaymentRequired JSON only to the `payment-required` header, leaving the body as `{}` — added with402Body() interceptor that decodes the header and emits the PaymentRequired as the body on 402; (c) resource.mimeType was empty — set `mimeType: 'application/json'` on both route configs. Live-verified on mnemo-production-c4f1.up.railway.app: GET/POST /mcp both return 402 with `https://` resource.url, `application/json` mimeType, and the full PaymentRequired JSON in the body. Test A (unpaid → 402) still passes. Commit d7902f8 pushed to master, Railway auto-deployed. Ready to resubmit to OKX.AI.
completed.4.14: Paid-path fix for OKX.AI second-round feedback (replayStatus=0, 'error sending request for url' on paid POST replay). Root cause: stubFacilitatorClient.verify() and settle() threw instead of returning proper response objects, and the middleware chain had no safety net for facilitator errors. Three fixes: (1) stub now returns {isValid:false,invalidReason:'stub_mode'} / {success:false,errorReason:'stub_mode'} so the SDK emits a proper 402 with error details; (2) with402Body() .catch()es any middleware error and returns a clean 402 with {x402Version:2,error,errorReason} — without this, a facilitator error caused the connection to die with no response; (3) with402Body() races the middleware against a 25s timeout so a slow web3.okx.com API returns a 402 instead of a transport-level hang. End-to-end verified with probe-paid-replay.ts against Railway: unpaid → 402, signed EIP-3009 payment → 200 with full MCP tools/list result (real OKXFacilitatorClient works from Railway). Commit 0f29ef5 pushed to master, Railway auto-deployed. replaySuccess=true. Ready to resubmit to OKX.AI.
